name: Question 4
problem: Let $X$ be the score obtained on the roll of a fair eight-sided die with sides labeled with numbers $1$ through $8.$ What is $\text{SD}[X]?$
worked_solution:
The standard deviation of a random variable $X$ is defined as

$$
\text{SD}[X]=\sqrt{\text{Var}[X]},
$$

where the variance can be computed using the following formula:

$$
\text{Var}[X]=\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2}
$$

First, we need to compute the probability mass function $f(x).$ Here, there are $8$ possible outcomes $(1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8)$ and each outcome has the same probability, so the probability mass function is as follows:

| $x$ | $1$ | $2$ | $3$ | $4$ | $5$ | $6$ | $7$ | $8$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x)$ | $\frac{1}{8}$ | $\frac{1}{8}$ | $\frac{1}{8}$ | $\frac{1}{8}$ | $\frac{1}{8}$ | $\frac{1}{8}$ | $\frac{1}{8}$ | $\frac{1}{8}$ |

Next, we compute $\text{E}[X].$ Summing up the products of each value of $X$ and its associated probability, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & =1\cdot f(1)+2\cdot f(2)+3\cdot f(3)+4\cdot f(4)+5\cdot f(5)+6\cdot f(6)+7\cdot f(7)+8\cdot f(8) \\  & =1(\frac{1}{8})+2(\frac{1}{8})+3(\frac{1}{8})+4(\frac{1}{8})+5(\frac{1}{8})+6(\frac{1}{8})+7(\frac{1}{8})+8(\frac{1}{8}) \\  & =\frac{9}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we compute $\text{E}[{X}^{2}].$ Summing up the products of each value of ${X}^{2}$ and its associated probability, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}] & ={1}^{2}\cdot f(1)+{2}^{2}\cdot f(2)+{3}^{2}\cdot f(3)+{4}^{2}\cdot f(4)+{5}^{2}\cdot f(5)+{6}^{2}\cdot f(6)+{7}^{2}\cdot f(7)+{8}^{2}\cdot f(8) \\  & =1(\frac{1}{8})+4(\frac{1}{8})+9(\frac{1}{8})+16(\frac{1}{8})+25(\frac{1}{8})+36(\frac{1}{8})+49(\frac{1}{8})+64(\frac{1}{8}) \\  & =\frac{51}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the variance is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2} \\  & =\frac{51}{2}-{(\frac{9}{2})}^{2} \\  & =\frac{51}{2}-\frac{81}{4} \\  & =\frac{21}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{SD}[X] & =\sqrt{\text{Var}[X]} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{21}{4}} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{21}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 4

Let X be the score obtained on the roll of a fair eight-sided die with sides labeled with numbers 1 through 8. What is SD[X]?

212

EXPLANATION

The standard deviation of a random variable X is defined as

SD[X]=Var[X],

where the variance can be computed using the following formula:

Var[X]=E[X2]−E[X]2

First, we need to compute the probability mass function f(x). Here, there are 8 possible outcomes (1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8) and each outcome has the same probability, so the probability mass function is as follows:

x 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8
f(x) 18 18 18 18 18 18 18 18

Next, we compute E[X]. Summing up the products of each value of X and its associated probability, we get

E[X]=1⋅f(1)+2⋅f(2)+3⋅f(3)+4⋅f(4)+5⋅f(5)+6⋅f(6)+7⋅f(7)+8⋅f(8)=1(18)+2(18)+3(18)+4(18)+5(18)+6(18)+7(18)+8(18)=92.

Then, we compute E[X2]. Summing up the products of each value of X2 and its associated probability, we get

E[X2]=12⋅f(1)+22⋅f(2)+32⋅f(3)+42⋅f(4)+52⋅f(5)+62⋅f(6)+72⋅f(7)+82⋅f(8)=1(18)+4(18)+9(18)+16(18)+25(18)+36(18)+49(18)+64(18)=512.

So, the variance is given by

Var[X]=E[X2]−E[X]2=512−(92)2=512−814=214.

Finally,

SD[X]=Var[X]=214=212.
